title: Critics warned about Flock surveillance. Three Houston-area investigations are fueling those concerns.

reports.title: Fort Bend County Sheriff's Office lieutenant admits to improper use of Flock cameras per docs
Critics warned about Flock surveillance. Three Houston-area investigations are fueling those concerns.

summary:
A Fort Bend County Sheriff's Office lieutenant improperly searched Flock camera records for two license plates, looking up one 41 times and the other 148 times between January 2022 and December 2025. The lieutenant admitted the searches were not for official law enforcement work. A resident had filed a complaint alleging the lieutenant was stalking them and that they feared for their family's safety. The lieutenant said he was concerned the two drivers were lurking near his home and family, and documents described a contentious familial relationship with one vehicle owner.

An internal affairs investigation found the lieutenant violated department rules and suspended him for two days. He is not facing criminal charges and said he did not use or share the information. ABC13 has contacted the lieutenant and the sheriff's office for comment and is awaiting a response.
